[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Without an automated structural check at the start of every CI/CD pipeline run, non-conforming code — including AI-generated code that deviates from an approved Golden Path — reaches test, scan, and deployment stages before the deviation is caught, wasting pipeline resources and allowing governance violations to accumulate silently.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

An Architecture Conformance Gate is a mandatory, fast-fail CI/CD pipeline stage that runs before any test, security scan, or deployment step. It validates that the repository structure, required files, dependency constraints, and compliance metadata annotations match the declared Golden Path for that workload class. Output that does not conform to any known Golden Path is blocked immediately and escalated to human architectural review.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Every CI/CD pipeline in the enterprise, regardless of whether the output was human-authored or AI-generated
- Any repository that declares a Golden Path in its metadata
- Any organization operating an autonomous AI development pipeline where human review cannot scale to verify every commit
page_texts.7:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Violations caught at build time cost minutes to fix; violations caught at runtime cost days to weeks
- Shifts governance from per-output human review to per-exception human review, scaling governance without scaling headcount
- Produces machine-readable conformance evidence at every build, creating an audit trail with no incremental effort per subsequent audit
page_texts.8:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#target-audience]

## Target Audience

This pattern is intended for the following technical roles:

- **Platform Engineer** — responsible for building and maintaining the shared infrastructure platform and conformance gate tooling
- **Infrastructure Architect** — designing and governing infrastructure patterns, conformance rules, and Golden Path standards
- **DevOps Engineer** — implementing and operating CI/CD pipelines that incorporate the conformance gate stage
- **Site Reliability Engineer (SRE)** — ensuring reliability and observability of the gate and escalation pipeline
page_texts.10:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Gainwell operates in a heavily regulated environment (HIPAA, FedRAMP, SOC 2, Medicaid) where architectural consistency and compliance traceability are audit requirements, not preferences. The [Enterprise Golden Path Strategy](../../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-golden-path-strategy.md) establishes a catalog of pre-approved, opinionated workload blueprints. That catalog's governance value depends entirely on whether systems built by developers — and increasingly by autonomous AI agents — actually conform to the declared path. Without a structural enforcement mechanism, the catalog is documentation, not governance.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

CI/CD pipelines at Gainwell execute on GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines. Each repository declares a workload class and a corresponding Golden Path. The conformance gate consumes the catalog's machine-readable index (structured YAML/JSON) to evaluate repositories. It runs before tests, before security scans, and before any deployment step.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

When AI agents generate application or infrastructure code, they produce structurally similar but not byte-for-byte identical output relative to the Golden Path template. Without a conformance gate, there is no systematic mechanism to detect structural deviations — missing required files, wrong directory structure, prohibited dependencies, absent compliance metadata — before the code is deployed. Human reviewers may catch some deviations; they will miss others, and they cannot review at AI generation speeds.
page_texts.13:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- Must be fast (< 60 seconds) to avoid becoming a developer friction point
- Must produce structured evidence output (JSON/YAML result artifact), not just pass/fail console output
- Must support exception workflow: output that fails the gate must have a clear escalation path to human architectural review, not simply a blocked pipeline with no recourse
- Must be extensible: new Golden Paths add new conformance rules without changes to the gate runner itself
page_texts.15:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

The Architecture Conformance Gate pattern implements a dedicated pipeline stage — positioned as the first substantive stage after checkout — that loads the Golden Path catalog, identifies the declared path for the repository, and evaluates the checked-out repository against the structural rules defined in the path's Verification Contract. A conformance report artifact is produced regardless of pass/fail. On failure, the pipeline halts and an exception review ticket is automatically created for architectural triage.
page_texts.16:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  CI/CD Pipeline                                                      │
│                                                                      │
│  ① Checkout  ──►  ② Conformance Gate  ──►  ③ Tests  ──►  ④ Deploy  │
│                         │                                            │
│               ┌─────────┴──────────┐                                │
│               │  Catalog Loader    │  ◄── Golden Path Catalog Index  │
│               │  Rule Evaluator    │  ◄── Verification Contract      │
│               │  Evidence Writer   │  ──► Conformance Report (JSON)  │
│               │  Exception Router  │  ──► ARB Ticket (on failure)    │
│               └────────────────────┘                                │
│                                                                      │
│   PASS: pipeline continues unmodified                                │
│   FAIL: pipeline halts, exception ticket created, team notified      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
page_texts.17:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Catalog Loader | Fetches the current Golden Path catalog index from the Platform Developer Portal | Golden Path Catalog (PTN-GOV-AI-001) |
| Rule Evaluator | Applies the Verification Contract rules for the declared Golden Path against the repository | Verification Contract (PTN-GOV-AI-003) |
| Evidence Writer | Produces a structured JSON conformance report artifact stored in the pipeline run record | Compliance Evidence Store (PTN-GOV-AI-004) |
| Exception Router | On gate failure, creates an architectural exception ticket and notifies the team and on-call architect | AI Governance Policy (PTN-GOV-AI-002) |
| Gate Runner | Orchestrates the above components as a reusable composite GitHub Action or Azure Pipelines task | CI/CD pipeline infrastructure |
page_texts.18:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. Pipeline checkout completes
2. Gate Runner invokes Catalog Loader to retrieve the current catalog version and the Verification Contract for the repository's declared Golden Path
3. Rule Evaluator runs each check in the Verification Contract sequentially; each check produces a pass/fail result with detail
4. Evidence Writer serializes all results into a structured JSON report and attaches it as a pipeline artifact
5. If all checks pass: gate exits 0, pipeline continues
6. If any check fails: Exception Router creates a triage ticket and gate exits non-zero, halting the pipeline
page_texts.19:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Warning-only mode**: Used during initial rollout or for repositories in migration; gate reports violations but does not halt the pipeline. Intended as a temporary transition state only — not a permanent configuration.
- **Scoped evaluation**: For monorepos, the gate evaluates only the changed service directory rather than the full repository, using a path-filter on the changed file list.
- **Multi-path support**: A repository may declare multiple Golden Paths for different service subdirectories. The gate evaluates each declared path independently.
page_texts.21:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- Golden Path Catalog published and accessible via machine-readable index endpoint (PTN-GOV-AI-001)
- Verification Contract defined for each Golden Path in the catalog (PTN-GOV-AI-003)
- Compliance Evidence Store operational and accepting pipeline artifacts (PTN-GOV-AI-004)
- Standard CI/CD pipeline template updated to include the gate stage
- Exception management process defined (how teams request architectural exception approval)
page_texts.23:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#phase-1-gate-infrastructure]

#### Phase 1: Gate Infrastructure

1. Build the Gate Runner as a reusable composite GitHub Action (`.github/actions/conformance-gate/`) or Azure Pipelines template task
2. Implement the Catalog Loader: HTTP fetch of the Golden Path catalog index from the Platform Developer Portal; cache with a TTL of 5 minutes
3. Implement the Rule Evaluator: file existence checks, directory structure validation, dependency manifest scanning, metadata annotation validation
4. Implement the Evidence Writer: serialize results to `conformance-report.json` matching the evidence store schema; attach as pipeline artifact
5. Implement the Exception Router: on failure, call the issue tracker API to create a triage ticket with the conformance report attached; notify on-call architect channel
page_texts.24:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#phase-2-pipeline-integration]

#### Phase 2: Pipeline Integration

1. Update the enterprise standard CI/CD pipeline template to include the conformance gate as stage 2 (after checkout)
2. Add `golden_path` metadata field to the standard repository `service.yaml` or `catalog-info.yaml` — this is the declaration the gate reads
3. Deploy gate to the first pilot team repositories in warning-only mode; monitor false positive rate
4. Tune rule implementations based on pilot findings; promote to fail-hard mode once false positive rate is < 1%
5. Roll out to all repositories via standard pipeline template update
page_texts.25:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#phase-3-organizational-rollout]

#### Phase 3: Organizational Rollout

1. Update the Platform Developer Portal documentation with gate behavior, exception process, and how to declare a Golden Path in repository metadata
2. Establish SLA for exception ticket response (recommended: 1 business day for architectural triage)
3. Begin reporting on gate pass rates by team and Golden Path class in the architecture metrics dashboard

[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#example-2-github-actions-gate-step]

#### Example 2: GitHub Actions Gate Step

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
jobs:
  build:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Architecture Conformance Gate
        uses: gainwell/actions/conformance-gate@v1
        with:
          catalog_url: ${{ vars.GOLDEN_PATH_CATALOG_URL }}
          mode: fail  # fail | warn
          evidence_store_url: ${{ vars.EVIDENCE_STORE_URL }}
          exception_tracker_url: ${{ vars.JIRA_API_URL }}
        env:
          CATALOG_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CATALOG_API_TOKEN }}
          EVIDENCE_STORE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.EVIDENCE_STORE_TOKEN }}

      - name: Run Tests
        # ... tests only run if conformance gate passed
```

page_texts.30:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#example-4-composite-action-internal-structure]

#### Example 4: Composite Action Internal Structure

The enterprise composite action wraps the gate scripts for reuse across all repositories:

```yaml
# .github/actions/conformance-gate/action.yml
name: 'Architecture Conformance Gate'
description: 'Validates repository structure against declared Golden Path Verification Contract'

inputs:
  catalog_version:
    description: 'Golden Path catalog version to evaluate against'
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  mode:
    description: 'Enforcement mode: warn or deny'
    required: false
    default: 'deny'
  evidence_store_url:
    description: 'URL of the Compliance Evidence Store to write reports to'
    required: true

outputs:
  result:
    description: 'Overall gate result: PASS or FAIL'
    value: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.result }}
  report_id:
    description: 'Unique ID of the conformance report written to the evidence store'
    value: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.report_id }}
  exception_ticket_url:
    description: 'URL of the auto-created exception ticket if gate failed'
    value: ${{ steps.exception.outputs.ticket_url }}

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Read Golden Path declaration
      id: read_declaration
      shell: bash
      run: |
        GOLDEN_PATH=$(python scripts/read-golden-path-declaration.py)
        echo "golden_path=$GOLDEN_PATH" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

    - name: Fetch Verification Contract
      id: fetch_contract
      shell: bash
      run: |
        python scripts/fetch-verification-contract.py \
          --path-id ${{ steps.read_declaration.outputs.golden_path }} \
          --catalog-version ${{ inputs.catalog_version }}

    - name: Run conformance checks
      id: gate
      shell: bash
      run: |
        python scripts/run-conformance-checks.py \
          --contract contract.yaml \
          --mode ${{ inputs.mode }} \
          --evidence-store ${{ inputs.evidence_store_url }}

    - name: Create exception ticket on failure
      id: exception
      if: steps.gate.outputs.result == 'FAIL' && inputs.mode == 'deny'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        python scripts/create-exception-ticket.py \
          --report-id ${{ steps.gate.outputs.report_id }}
```

**Usage in team repository:**
```yaml
- name: Architecture Conformance Gate
  uses: gainwell-platform/actions/conformance-gate@v2
  with:
    mode: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'deny' || 'warn' }}
    evidence_store_url: ${{ vars.EVIDENCE_STORE_URL }}
```
page_texts.31:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Version the gate itself alongside the catalog; a catalog version bump may require gate rule updates
- During initial rollout, use warning-only mode for 2–4 weeks to baseline the false positive rate before switching to fail-hard
- Treat exception tickets as a signal: high exception rates for a specific Golden Path indicate the path needs refinement, not that teams need more discipline
- Store conformance reports for the full evidence retention period (3 years minimum for HIPAA/FedRAMP scope) regardless of pass/fail result
page_texts.32:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Gate placed after tests**: Positions conformance check too late — tests for non-conforming output waste time and may produce misleading results. Gate must be first.
- **Warning-only as permanent state**: Warning-only mode provides visibility without enforcement. Teams learn to ignore warnings. Set a firm date to switch to fail-hard mode during rollout.
- **Rules encoding style opinions**: Conformance rules must encode Golden Path structural requirements, not code style preferences. Style belongs in linters. Gate rules that are subjective generate disputes and erode trust in the gate.
- **No exception process defined before gate goes live**: Teams blocked by the gate with no clear path forward will route around it. Define and publish the exception process before enabling fail-hard mode.

- Conformance reports must be retained for a minimum of 3 years for HIPAA and FedRAMP audit purposes

### Approval Process

The gate runner and its rule implementations require ARB approval before deployment to production pipelines. Changes to the rule evaluation logic for any Golden Path require the same review as changes to the Golden Path itself.

[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#real-world-example-1]

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** The benefits-platform team adopts the `HIPAA-REST-MICROSERVICE-AKS-V1` Golden Path for a new eligibility API service. An AI agent generates the initial scaffold.

**Implementation:** The conformance gate runs on the first pull request and catches two violations: a missing OpenAPI specification file and a PHI data field with no HIPAA annotation. The gate fails, an exception ticket is created, and the team receives a notification with the full conformance report. The AI agent is re-invoked with corrected context; the second run passes.

**Outcome:** Violations caught before code review, before testing, before any security scan — at the lowest-cost remediation point in the pipeline.
page_texts.40:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#real-world-example-2]

### Real-World Example 2

**Context:** A developer manually authors a Scheduled Batch Job service without using the approved Golden Path scaffold, resulting in structural deviation.

**Implementation:** The conformance gate catches the structural deviation on the developer's first pull request. The gate report specifies exactly which checks failed and links to the Golden Path getting-started guide. The developer corrects the structure using the scaffold before requesting review.

**Outcome:** Code reviewer receives a pull request that has already passed structural conformance validation. Review time is focused on business logic and semantic correctness — the reviewer does not need to verify structural compliance manually.
page_texts.41:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#real-world-example-3]

### Real-World Example 3

**Context:** The provider-data team manages a monorepo containing 4 services: a REST API (GP-001), a batch job (GP-002), a data pipeline (GP-003), and a shared library (no path). Each sub-path requires different conformance rules, and the shared library should not be evaluated against any Golden Path.

**Implementation:** The `service.yaml` at each sub-path root declares its Golden Path independently: `services/api/service.yaml` declares `GP-001`, `services/batch/service.yaml` declares `GP-002`, etc. The `services/shared-lib/service.yaml` declares `golden_path: none`. The conformance gate reads each sub-path's declaration and evaluates it independently. The GitHub Actions workflow uses a matrix strategy to run 4 parallel gate evaluations — one per sub-path. The shared library gate is a no-op pass.

**Outcome:** The monorepo passes the conformance gate in 90 seconds with 4 parallel evaluations. Each team sees their service conformance result independently. The batch job fails (missing `job-config.yaml`); the other 3 pass. Only the batch job path is blocked from merging.

[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#scenario-1-autonomous-ai-pipeline-gate]

#### Scenario 1: Autonomous AI Pipeline Gate

An autonomous AI agent generates a complete microservice stack from a structured intent document. The conformance gate is the first automated check after generation. If the gate fails, the pipeline does not proceed to tests or deployment — the failure is routed back to the agent context pipeline for regeneration with corrected instructions.
page_texts.44:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#scenario-2-migration-rollout]

#### Scenario 2: Migration Rollout

Existing services not yet on a Golden Path are onboarded to the gate in warning-only mode. The gate reports identify structural gaps that the team resolves over a 4-week migration sprint before the gate switches to fail-hard mode.
page_texts.45:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#scenario-3-false-positive-tuning]

#### Scenario 3: False Positive Tuning

During the warning-only pilot with the eligibility team, the conformance gate fires 12 times per week on a `SC-005` rule that checks for a `docs/adr/` directory. Investigation reveals: the team stores ADRs in `docs/architecture/decisions/` (a valid variant allowed by the Golden Path prose but not captured in the conformance rule). Rather than marking all 12 firings as exceptions, the Platform Engineering team updates the `SC-005` rule to allow either path. The false positive rate drops to zero for this rule. After several tuning iterations the false positive rate drops below the 1% fail-hard promotion threshold.
page_texts.47:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

- **Deviation detection**: Architectural deviations reach code review, security scan, and sometimes deployment before being caught; each pipeline stage advanced increases remediation cost significantly
- **AI-generated output trust**: AI-generated scaffolds that deviate from the intended pattern are indistinguishable from conformant ones at code review time; structural verification requires human memory of the Golden Path specification
- **Compliance evidence**: Each compliance audit requires manually assembling PR comments and Confluence notes to demonstrate structural conformance for relevant services
- **Review scope**: Human reviewers spend time verifying structural requirements (directory layout, file naming, required configs) that are purely mechanical and can be automated
page_texts.48:
[patterns/infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

- **Deviation detection**: Structural deviations are caught in < 90 seconds on the first pipeline run — before any test runs, security scans, or human review time is spent on non-conforming output
- **AI-generated output trust**: AI-generated and human-authored code is held to the same conformance gate; conformance is machine-verified by construction, not asserted by human review
- **Compliance evidence**: Conformance reports are generated for every pipeline run and written to the Evidence Store; audit evidence is a structured query covering 100% of builds
- **Review scope**: Human reviewers focus entirely on semantic correctness, business logic, and security concerns — not structural compliance verification

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Non-conforming code — including AI-generated output — reaches expensive pipeline stages (tests, scans, deployment) before structural deviations from the approved Golden Path are detected.

**Solution:** A mandatory, fast-fail CI/CD stage positioned before all other stages that validates repository structure against the declared Golden Path's Verification Contract and produces machine-readable conformance evidence.

**When to Use:**
- Every CI/CD pipeline in the enterprise
- Any repository operating under Golden Path catalog governance
- Any team or pipeline using autonomous AI development

**Key Benefits:**
- Violations caught in < 90 seconds at the cheapest possible remediation point
- Scales governance from per-output human review to per-exception human review
- Produces continuous, automatic compliance evidence by construction

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium

**Prerequisites:** Golden Path Catalog (PTN-GOV-AI-001), Verification Contract (PTN-GOV-AI-003), Compliance Evidence Store (PTN-GOV-AI-004)

**Related Patterns:** PTN-GOV-AI-001, PTN-GOV-AI-003, PTN-GOV-AI-004, PTN-INFRA-GOV-002, PTN-APP-GOV-001
